page: Google Cloud Platform n4-highcpu-16 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an Intel processor featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs (8 physical cores with 2 threads per core) and 32.0 GB of system memory. This configuration provides a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_tile, AMX_int8) and Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512). This server does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it is provisioned with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark testing, the n4-highcpu-16 demonstrates solid compute capabilities with a stress-ng single-core score of 1781.09 and a multi-core score of 14630.37. Its memory subsystem achieves a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 1133.53 GB/sec, which drops to 130.97 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, alongside a write bandwidth of 72.76 GB/sec. The system records a Geekbench multi-core score of 11411.0, with specific sub-test results including 16070.0 for software compilation with Clang and 19410.0 for ray tracing. For database and web operations, the server handles Redis SET operations at 17.79 million operations per second and delivers a static web serving throughput of 25.59 GB/sec.

The primary tradeoff of the n4-highcpu-16 is its compute-heavy, memory-lean ratio of 2 GB of RAM per vCPU, which limits its utility for memory-intensive databases or large-scale data caching. Additionally, the complete absence of local NVMe storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which may impact I/O-heavy operations. However, the inclusion of Intel AMX instructions enables efficient low-precision AI inference, achieving 1272.6 tokens per second for prompt processing on a small 135M parameter LLM and 88.94 tokens per second on a medium 7B model. This makes the instance highly cost-efficient for compute-bound workloads such as software compilation, web serving, text processing, and lightweight machine learning inference.

Lacking local storage and GPU accelerators, it relies on network storage. The processor features a 260 MB L3 cache and supports Intel AMX and AVX-512 instructions. In benchmarks, it achieves a Geekbench multi-core score of 11411.0, a stress-ng multi-core score of 14630.37, and processes Redis SET operations at 17.79 million operations per second. It also handles small-model LLM prompt processing at 1272.6 tokens per second. This instance is designed for compute-bound tasks, including software compilation, static web serving, and lightweight AI inference, offering a resource-dense profile that minimizes memory overhead costs.
